original_question: How can nature-inspired optimization algorithms handle nonlinear constraints effectively in constrained optimization problems?
target_in_paper: The draft most closely matches the additional unnumbered open problem stated in the concluding paragraph of Section 4.5, immediately after Open Problem 5: "how to deal with nonlinear constraints effectively." The intended scope is clarified by the Abstract, Section 1, and Section 4.3.
correct_elements: The draft correctly identifies the relevant algorithmic family (nature-inspired optimization algorithms), the central issue (effective handling of nonlinear constraints), and the constrained-optimization setting. It is already very close to the paper's own wording and does not drift into unrelated topics.
missing_details: The paper poses this as an additional unnumbered open problem at the end of Section 4.5, not as one of the five numbered open problems.

The motivating problem class is not generic constrained optimization in the abstract; it is real-world optimization problems with highly nonlinear, multimodal objective landscapes subject to complex nonlinear constraints.

Section 4.3 adds an important hidden assumption about scope: the relevant feasible domains may be irregular and can even consist of many isolated regions or islands, unlike standard regular benchmark domains.

The paper frames the issue partly as a benchmarking gap: many benchmark functions are unconstrained or only simply constrained, so good benchmark performance may not transfer to realistic nonlinear-constraint settings.

A faithful stand-alone rewrite should not invent formal notation, specific constraint classes, or particular techniques (such as penalties, repairs, barriers, or feasibility rules), because the paper itself states the problem only at a high level.

No ambient ring or field, variable list, operator definitions, homogeneity assumptions, degree restrictions, nilpotency conditions, or asymptotic quantifiers such as 'for all sufficiently large m' appear in this paper for this problem; those items are not applicable here.
refined_question: In real-world constrained optimization problems whose objective landscapes are highly nonlinear and multimodal, and whose feasible sets are defined by complex nonlinear constraints that may produce irregular domains or many isolated feasible regions, how can nature-inspired optimization algorithms be made to deal with those nonlinear constraints effectively, rather than only performing well on unconstrained or simply constrained benchmark problems?
justification: The paper arXiv:2003.03776 does not contain a Conjecture 1.1, Proposition 1.2, or Theorem 1.3. Instead, the draft matches an unnumbered open problem stated verbatim at the end of Section 4.5: "how to deal with nonlinear constraints effectively." The Abstract and Section 1 explain that the paper is concerned with optimization problems arising in science and engineering that are highly nonlinear, often multimodal, and subject to complex nonlinear constraints. Section 4.3 sharpens the intended scope by emphasizing that real application problems may have irregular feasible domains and even many isolated regions, unlike the unconstrained or simply constrained benchmark functions commonly used in the literature. Because the paper gives this problem only as a verbal open direction, the refined question should preserve that level of generality while making the application context and feasible-domain issues explicit.
